The notion of affect (affectation 2) has the advantage of being inscribed in an intellectual tradition that brings original answers to the questions of the origins of attachment (and detachment) and of the mechanism by which it occurs. Notably, it emphasizes the role of the body in the way agents and their environment are articulated, which is crucial for understanding both how market agencements and mechanisms of attachment function. Pragmatist psychology managed to capture this tradition and express it in terms well adapted to the analysis of commercial transactions. To be affected by something or someone (affectation 2) “corresponds to the subject becoming aware of corporeal modifications triggered by apprehending certain objects or facts.”

To be convinced of this, “it is enough to imagine an emotion and to make a thought experiment consisting in subtracting all bodily feelings from it; there is nothing left but a cold and neutral intellectual state.”

Emotion is a corporeal relation to the other. The result is that the affected agent becomes aware of this articulation with the world and of its effects on him. The entwinement of body and spirit refutes Cartesianism and the short-circuit it establishes between the world and thought. It allows us to understand how a meeting organized with goods, affectation 1, must affect agents, affectation 2, in order to lead to a commercial transaction. The word “affect” does justice to the action of things and beings on the agent.

情动（affectation 2，即感发）这一概念的好处在于，它属于一个思想传统，而这个传统对附着（以及脱离）的起源问题、对其发生机制的问题给出了独到的回答。尤其重要的是，它强调身体在行动者与其环境相互接合的方式中所起的作用；这对于理解市场装配与附着机制二者如何运作都至关重要。实用主义心理学成功地把握了这一传统，并用很适合分析商业交易的语言把它表达出来。被某物或某人触动（affectation 2，感发），“对应于主体觉察到由把握某些对象或事实所引发的身体变化”。
要确信这一点，“只需想象一种情绪，并做一个思想实验：从中减去一切身体感觉；剩下的便只是一个冷淡而中性的智性状态”。
情绪是一种与他者的身体性关系。其结果是，被触动的行动者觉察到自己与世界的这种接合，以及这种接合对他产生的效应。身体与精神的缠绕驳倒了笛卡尔主义，以及它在世界与思想之间建立的那种短路。它使我们得以理解：经组织而发生的与物品的相遇（affectation 1，指派）必须如何触动行动者（affectation 2，感发），才能导向一场商业交易。“情动”一词恰如其分地表达了物与存在者对行动者的作用。

The dynamics of attachment always begin with a question, with something troubling the agent: he is perturbed by what he is faced with, by what is being offered to him. A seller runs through his pitch — think back to the street vendors; an advertisement upsets conventional wisdom; a start-up offers an original molecule. When everything is running smoothly, when things and actions are repeated again and again in an identical way, the question of attachment will not arise: the devices for trust will suffice to guarantee the transaction. The goods are there; they have uses, values, qualities. They are acquired or not out of habit. In the face of a new event, however, in a new situation that is not reducible to any known situation, the agent must figure out a response. He has to face questions as elementary and fundamental as “What will this good do to me?” “Will this profile on Meetic suit me to such an extent that I will not be able to do without it, that it will hold onto me as tightly as I will hold onto it?” “Is this new treatment profiled for me, will it become part of my life, become the regimen I adopt?” In order to reclaim some serenity, a certain equilibrium, the agent has to investigate and experiment. And if the good does (sometimes) end up being indispensable, it is because the agent gradually becomes attached to it over the course of the investigation. The inevitable tension between the agent and the good is resolved only by their simultaneous transformation and adaptation. And it is over the course of this process, which takes the form of an investigation saturated with affectation 2, that the agent elaborates a discourse on the motives of his attachment.

附着的动态总是始于一个问题，始于某种搅扰行动者的东西：他为自己所面对之物、为被提供给他之物所困扰。一名卖家滔滔不绝地念完自己的推销词——回想一下那些街头卖家；一则广告扰乱了常识；一家初创企业提供了一种独创的分子。当一切顺利运转，当物与行动以完全相同的方式一再重复时，附着的问题就不会出现：信任装置便足以保证交易。物品就在那里；它们有用途、有价值、有品质。人们出于习惯购买它们，或者不购买。然而，面对一个新事件，面对一个不能化约为任何已知情境的新情境，行动者必须设法作出回应。他不得不面对一些既基本又根本的问题：“这件物品会对我做什么？”“Meetic 上的这个用户画像会与我契合到这种地步吗——以至于我离不开它，它抓住我，正如我抓住它一样紧？”“这种新疗法是为我量身定制的吗？它会成为我生活的一部分、成为我所采纳的治疗方案吗？”为了重获几分安宁、某种平衡，行动者必须探究、实验。而如果物品（有时）最终变得不可或缺，那是因为行动者在探究过程中逐渐附着于它。行动者与物品之间不可避免的张力，只有通过二者同时的转化与适应才得以化解。正是在这一过程之中——它采取一种充满感发（affectation 2）的探究形式——行动者建构起一套关于自己附着动机的话语。

A central part in this exploration is verbalizing — putting into words. Consider the example of a meal where the wine on offer becomes the subject of a conversation among the guests. What should they think of this bottle? The collective investigation (a prototype of all the investigations of the same type at larger scales) takes the form of a conversation that makes reference to the label, the color, that invites tasting and commenting and generates comments that are in turn commented on. Opinions and debates follow each other, answering to one another, are interrupted by all sorts of tests and demonstrations. The wine, its bouquet, the length of its finish express themselves, little by little, as they are expressed by each participant in the conversation. Sometimes a way of seeing, feeling, speaking that is local, but of course feeds on prior conversations or readings, manages to be established. At the end of this exchange, which is a test both for the guests and for the wine, it is no longer the same wine that is drunk, and the guests who drink it are not the same either. Everyone has changed, at least to a certain extent. A community of wine enthusiasts has taken shape. The words that come to the amateurs’ minds are important in the dynamic of these changes and in their expression. But one should not forget the wine, which, by affecting their bodies, participates actively in this putting into words, loosening tongues and getting the guests to speak. Our bodies resonate and our minds reason; that is, in sum, what William James tells us. It is obvious that goods count in the shaping and expression of attachments because they act on bodies that learn to be affected by them. If agents are capable of such reflexivity (“I really like what I like”), it is because the process of attachment is also a process of expression over the course of which they learn what they are and what they are becoming and, symmetrically, over the course of which things and goods express what they are or what they can be and what they can make others do (the term in French is
faire faire

). It is not the case that there exist, on the one hand, things and the world, and on the other hand, representations and words to speak of them. Words and things are interwoven, like macramé. The exchange of goods cannot be dissociated from the exchange of words.

在这一探索中，一个核心环节是言语化，即把事物化为词语。不妨以一顿饭为例：席间供应的葡萄酒成为宾客们交谈的主题。他们该怎样看待这瓶酒？集体探究（所有在更大规模上进行的同类探究的原型）采取一场交谈的形式：交谈提及酒标、颜色，邀请人品尝并评论，并产生出又被进一步评论的评论。意见与争论相继而来、彼此应答，又被各种各样的检验与演示打断。葡萄酒、它的酒香、它余味的悠长，一点一点地自我表达出来，同时也被交谈中的每一位参与者表达出来。有时，一种局部的看、感、说的方式得以确立下来——当然，它汲取自先前的交谈或阅读。在这场交流结束时——这场交流对宾客和葡萄酒双方都是一场考验——被喝掉的不再是同一款酒，喝它的宾客也不再是原来的宾客。每个人都变了，至少在一定程度上变了。一个葡萄酒爱好者的共同体成形了。在这些变化及其表达的动态中，爱好者们脑海中浮现的词语是重要的。但也不应忘记葡萄酒：它通过触动他们的身体，积极地参与到这种化为词语的过程中，使人们打开话匣子，让宾客们开口说话。我们的身体在共鸣，我们的心智在推理；总之，这就是威廉·詹姆斯（William James）告诉我们的。显而易见，物品在附着的塑成与表达中举足轻重，因为它们作用于那些学会被它们触动的身体。如果行动者能够具有这样的反身性（“我确实喜欢我所喜欢的东西”），那是因为附着过程同时也是一个表达过程：在此过程中，他们认识到自己是什么、正在成为什么；而对称地，在此过程中，物与物品也表达出它们是什么、能够成为什么，以及能够使他人做什么（法语中的说法是
faire faire
）。并不是一方面存在着物与世界，另一方面存在着表象与谈论它们的词语。词与物交织在一起，如同马克拉梅编织（macramé）一般。物品的交换不能与词语的交换相分离。

Borrowed from Antoine Hennion, who has made a decisive contribution to this current of analysis, the preceding illustration summarizes what recent work devoted to the attachment process has taught us.

Yes, as Franck Cochoy emphasizes, things matter — they are concerns, they affect agents, and they incite investigation. The agents are affected, however, only if they have learned or have been taught to be affected. Verbal exchanges, which articulate precepts and concepts, play a central role in this learning. Attachment is a matter of conversation, and like the latter, it is a matter of know-how.
上述例子借自安托万·埃尼翁（Antoine Hennion），他对这一分析潮流作出了决定性的贡献；这个例子概括了晚近关于附着过程的研究教给我们的东西。
是的，正如弗兰克·科舒瓦（Franck Cochoy）所强调的，物是重要的——它们是关切，它们触动行动者，并激发探究。然而，行动者只有在已经学会或被教会如何被触动的情况下，才会被触动。言语交流把准则与概念接合起来，在这一学习中起着核心作用。附着是一件关乎交谈的事，而且与交谈一样，它是一件关乎诀窍（know-how）的事。

Luckily, the attachment process is a structured process that can be organized from the moment goods trouble agents through to the investigations this provokes. Over the course of these investigations, affects are produced, identities transformed and connected, durable connections made, and solid associations between goods and agents established. This requires designing and implementing devices that give goods and agents the time and space to surprise and be surprised. The requirement of devices becomes all the more pressing as the singularization of products becomes more important and implies more intensive innovation. In order to be accepted and integrated in social life, goods forcefully demand pliable frameworks within which to unfold and deploy so as to produce emotions and affect agents rendered curious, receptive, and attentive.

幸运的是，附着过程是一个有结构的过程，从物品开始搅扰行动者的那一刻起，直到由此引发的种种探究，它都可以被组织起来。在这些探究的过程中，情动被生产出来，身份被转化并彼此连接，持久的关系得以建立，物品与行动者之间牢固的结合得以确立。这要求设计并实施一些装置，为物品与行动者提供时间和空间，使它们既能出人意料，也能遭遇意外。随着产品的独一化变得更为重要并意味着更为密集的创新，对装置的需要也变得愈发紧迫。为了被接受并融入社会生活，物品强烈地要求有柔韧的框架，好让它们在其中展开、施展，以生产情绪，并触动那些被弄得好奇、易于接受且专注的行动者。

Sociologist Emmanuel Kessous’s research provides a good illustration of devices that function in attachment, as well as of the tight connections they must weave between affectation 1 and affectation 2.

On the dating platform he studies, candidates are first required to engage with profiling operations that allow users to evaluate and classify the different participants. Next comes a period of bilateral relations, which, after a number of twists and turns, end up becoming concrete in the form of a relationship that will be a fleeting affair for some or possibly, as the protagonists hope, could last a lifetime. Nothing is given at the start; everything must be acquired. Attachment is gradual, built up through successive trials. It progresses with each step of the investigation that the protagonists lead as they set off to discover, or rather I should say to invent, not only themselves and others, but also the type of relationship they will cement. This investigation would be impossible if it were not framed, channeled, and structured by the platform, its technologies, its algorithms, its categories. This sociotechnical platform constitutes an almost pure form of attachment device. The investigation provokes surprise, generates speech, organizes trials, stages bodies that express themselves, first through photographs and words, then eventually through physical meetings.
社会学家埃马纽埃尔·凯苏斯（Emmanuel Kessous）的研究，为在附着中发挥作用的装置，以及这些装置必须在指派（affectation 1）与感发（affectation 2）之间编织的紧密联系，提供了一个很好的例证。

在他所研究的约会平台上，候选人首先必须参与画像操作，这些操作使用户得以评估并分类不同的参与者。接下来是一段双边关系的时期；经过若干波折之后，这段关系最终以某种结合的形式落到实处——对一些人来说，它是一段短暂的恋情；也可能如当事人所希望的那样，持续一生。开始时没有任何东西是现成的；一切都必须争取获得。附着是渐进的，通过接连不断的考验逐步建立起来。它随着当事人在探究中每迈出一步而推进——他们出发去发现，或者我毋宁说去发明，不仅是自身与他人，还有他们将要缔结的那种关系类型。这一探究若非由平台及其技术、算法与类别加以框定、导引和结构化，便不可能进行。这一社会技术平台构成了几乎是纯粹的附着装置形式。这一探究引发惊讶，催生言语，组织考验，并把那些自我表达的身体搬上舞台——先是借助照片与文字，最终则借助面对面的会面。

What happens on dating platforms has its equivalents in the analog world. Take Jacques Séguéla, the man behind advertising campaigns for Citroën and the campaign for Carte Noire coffee, “a coffee named desire.” When he invited Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni to a dinner he had organized, his modus operandi was like a platform analogous to that of Meetic. The same operations took place (profiling, self-presentation, conversations that swerved into the intimate register), which led to a lasting affair (“Carla and me, it’s serious,” Sarkozy famously said), although it could have ended with a shorter encounter. Séguéla does not work with multitudes, which makes his matchmaking role harder and more uncertain, but the stakes are the same: manufacturing attachments and consequently setting up a device that prepares and performs attachments.

约会平台上发生的事情，在线下世界中也有其对等物。以雅克·塞格拉（Jacques Séguéla）为例：他是雪铁龙（Citroën）系列广告的操刀者，也是 Carte Noire 咖啡“名为欲望的咖啡”这一广告活动的策划人。当他邀请尼古拉·萨科齐（Nicolas Sarkozy）与卡拉·布吕尼（Carla Bruni）参加他筹办的一场晚宴时，他的行事方式就像一个类似于 Meetic 的平台。同样的操作发生了（画像制作、自我呈现、转入私密语域的交谈），并导致了一段持久的关系（萨科齐那句名言：“卡拉和我，我们是认真的”），尽管它本来也可能以一次更短暂的相遇告终。塞格拉并不与诸众打交道，这使他的撮合角色更为困难、更不确定，但赌注是一样的：制造附着，并因而搭建一个为附着作准备并使之实现的装置。

There is a common perception among purists that dating platforms are contaminated by commercial models. Yet as I am arguing here, the supposed opposition and incompatibility between an impersonal commercial world and the world of emotions, passions, and attachments does not exist. Once participants have been profiled and the possibility of making connections has been organized, they do not have to institute a new space to reengage in authentic relationships. Dating platforms demonstrate that attachments have a role to play in the dynamics of commercial transactions: without attachments and the devices that produce them, supply and demand remain abstract, disembodied notions. Kessous irrefutably shows that contrary to what a long critical tradition has sustained, the market does not exclude personal relations. As economic sociologist Viviana Zelizer has magnificently shown, not only does the market enrich and color preexisting relations, it also constantly creates new ones, which it multiplies and nourishes. In a striking shortcut, Cochoy synthesizes this movement by putting forward two complementary notions — collection and selection. Understood as both actions and as results, these notions account for the fact that markets make relations between agents and goods proliferate, which generates collection, while attempting to rarify them through successive selection.

纯粹主义者中间有一种常见的看法：约会平台被商业模型所污染。然而，正如我在此所论证的，所谓非人格化的商业世界与情感、激情和附着的世界之间的对立与不相容并不存在。一旦参与者的画像被建立起来，建立联系的可能性被组织起来，他们就不必再设立一个新的空间来重新投入真实的关系。约会平台表明，附着在商业交易的动态中有一席之地：没有附着以及生产附着的装置，供给与需求便始终是抽象的、脱离身体的概念。凯苏斯无可辩驳地表明，与悠久的批判传统所主张的相反，市场并不排斥个人关系。正如经济社会学家维维安娜·泽利泽（Viviana Zelizer）出色地表明的，市场不仅丰富并渲染既有的关系，还不断创造新的关系，使之增殖、得到滋养。科舒瓦以一种引人注目的简捷方式，通过提出两个互补的概念——收集与选择——综合了这一运动。这两个概念既被理解为行动，也被理解为结果；它们说明了这样的事实：市场使行动者与物品之间的关系增殖，使关系汇集起来，同时又试图通过接连不断的选择使这些关系逐渐减少。

In this analysis, the bodies of things and people play a privileged part in the constitution and expression of affects and in the transformative process of attachment. Some will ask whether such an analysis can be transposed to market agencements, which, as we have seen, are peopled by qualculative agencies, equipped and matched, and which therefore are never or only exceptionally in direct contact with things. The example of Meetic (or of Séguéla the matchmaker) allows this question to be answered in the affirmative. Yes, agencies have bodies. To accommodate this observation, I would like to introduce the classical notion of a
sensorium

, which refers to the entire set of modalities of perception through which an organism experiences and interprets its environment. In the case of unequipped human beings, the sensorium designates the perceptions provided by the five senses, perceptions that affect the subject and lead it, through verbalization, to give meaning to the things that it encounters that move it. Yet the idea of a sensorium can easily be applied to qualculative agencies. Through their equipment, they also feel, perceive, and express themselves. Newton got it right when he introduced the idea that time and space are the
sensorium dei

. He thus reconciled his view of space-time as a fixed and independent reality with the existence of an omniscient and eternal God without having to worry about their respective places. Space and time, he said, are God’s equipment. They ensure his presence in the world without drowning him in the world, and at each point in space and time, they allow him to perceive what is happening and be affected by it. In fact, Newton speaks of space as “affection.”
Agencies (starting with God himself) are equipped, and their equipment is the sensorium. In general, distributed equipment constitutes the flesh, spirit, and soul of agencies.
在这一分析中，物与人的身体在情动的构成与表达中，在附着的转化过程中，扮演着特殊的角色。有人会问，这样的分析能否移植到市场装配之上——如我们所见，市场装配中栖居着质算能动者，它们被装备、被配对，因此从不或仅在例外情况下与物直接接触。Meetic（或作为撮合者的塞格拉）的例子使人可以对这个问题作肯定的回答。是的，能动者有身体。为了容纳这一观察，我想引入“感觉中枢”（
sensorium
）这一古典概念，它指一个有机体借以经验并解释其环境的全部感知模态。就未受装备的人类存在者而言，感觉中枢指五种感官所提供的知觉；这些知觉触动主体，并通过言语化，引导主体为那些触动它的、它所遭遇的事物赋予意义。然而，感觉中枢这一观念可以轻易地应用于质算能动者。通过它们的装备，它们同样在感受、知觉并表达自身。牛顿引入时间与空间是“上帝的感觉中枢”（
sensorium dei
）这一观念，他做得对。他由此把自己关于时空是固定而独立之实在的观点，与一位全知而永恒的上帝的存在调和起来，而不必操心二者各自的位置。他说，空间与时间就是上帝的装备。它们确保上帝临在于世界之中，又不使他淹没于世界之中；在空间与时间的每一点上，它们都使他得以知觉正在发生之事，并被其触动。事实上，牛顿把空间称为一种“情状”（affection）。
能动者（首先从上帝本身开始）是被装备的，而它们的装备就是感觉中枢。一般而言，分布式的装备构成了能动者的肉身、精神与灵魂。

Consider a company and its bookkeeping, some of which is founded on double-entry methods, a widely disseminated instrument that captures, processes, and interprets data and structures the affects of the company as agency. We say that BP or Total are
affected

by the oil crisis, plummeting prices, or Saudi Arabia’s strategy in making American fracking nonviable. The processes of affecting qualculative agencies, these assemblages of human bodies and other materials capable of perceiving, verbalizing, asking about the decisions to be made, capable of attaching or detaching, are similar to those of human beings totally stripped down, those naked bodies disarmed. What changes is the composition of the sensorium. Users of the platform on the French dating site Adopteunmec (the name means “adopt a guy”) are obviously not placed in a to face-to-face encounter the way Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni were during the famous meal that started their union and their mutual attachment. The person who engages on the platform is a sort of cyborg; it is only much later that they will stare into the eyes of the person selected after a first evaluation, a first scoring. Meanwhile, the platform of space-time where qualculations are made is their sensorium, as it collects and formats information, makes associations, syntheses, classifications, and hierarchies. In fact, if one thinks about it, a relationship between a human body and an object of attachment that involves no pomp or finery is quite the exception. Around Séguéla’s table laid for dinner there is much equipment.
不妨考虑一家公司及其簿记，其中一部分以复式记账法为基础；这是一种广为传播的工具，它捕捉、处理并解释数据，并结构着作为能动者的公司的情动。我们说，英国石油（BP）或道达尔（Total）受到了石油危机、价格暴跌，或沙特阿拉伯使美国水力压裂开采在经济上难以为继的战略的
触动

。触动质算能动者——这些由人体与其他材料组成、能够知觉、言语化、追问有待作出的决定、能够附着或脱离的集合体——的过程，与触动那些被彻底剥除的人类存在者的过程相似，与那些赤裸的、被解除武装的身体相似。发生变化的是感觉中枢的构成。法国约会网站 Adopteunmec（该名意为“收养一个男人”）的平台用户，显然不像尼古拉·萨科齐与卡拉·布吕尼在那场开启二人结合与相互附着的著名晚宴上那样，被置于面对面的相遇之中。在平台上投入其中的那个人是一种赛博格；要等到很久以后，他们才会凝视那个在初次评估、初次打分之后被选中之人的眼睛。在此期间，质算得以进行的那个时空平台就是他们的感觉中枢，因为它收集并格式化信息，进行联结、综合、分类与排序。事实上，如果细想一下，人体与附着对象之间不借助任何排场或装饰的关系，是相当罕见的。在塞格拉那张为晚宴铺好的餐桌周围，有许许多多的装备。

This analysis shows that attachment is inscribed in a process that is an extension of the previous framings I have presented. Attachments require a pass(act)ivated good (here, this good is put into relation with another being); they require qualculative agencies that evaluate profiles; and they also require more and more intimate meetings, which allow for adjustments and matches and which, at the same time, prepare for attachment. As I have insisted, to be effective, affectation 2 can never be completely dissociated from affectation 1.
这一分析表明，附着被铭刻在一个过程之中，而这个过程是我先前呈现的那些框定的延伸。附着需要一件被动化—激活的物品（在此，这件物品被置于与另一个存在者的关系之中）；附着需要评估画像的质算能动者；附着还需要越来越亲密的会面——这些会面容许调整与配对，同时也为附着作准备。正如我一再强调的，感发（affectation 2）若要有效，就绝不能与指派（affectation 1）完全分离。

Companies have understood the value of this connection very well, especially on digital platforms. To avoid any cooling off, messages are sent within a millisecond of a customer’s arrival on a site so as to reorient them toward other purchases before their possible departure. This is called retargeting. A manager explained to me that this rerouting requires no fewer than eight hundred employees, most of whom are mathematicians, and several hundred million euros in funding. This is no longer a matter of the alchemy of feelings, but rather of algebra. Passions, emotions, and affects are carried in and channeled by algorithms that circulate them in networks. I will now turn my attention toward attachment devices that are closely intertwined with the devices that handle the encounters of qualculative agencies.

企业非常懂得这种连接的价值，在数字平台上尤其如此。为了避免任何冷却，顾客一到达网站，消息便在毫秒之内发出，以便在他们可能离开之前把他们重新导向其他购买。这被称为重定向（retargeting）。一位经理向我解释，这种改道需要不少于八百名员工——其中大多数是数学家——以及数亿欧元的资金。这不再是情感炼金术的问题，而是代数的问题。激情、情绪与情动被算法承载、被算法导引，由算法在网络中流通。现在，我将把注意力转向那些与处理质算能动者相遇的装置紧密交织在一起的附着装置。

One last word before we leave this section. There is, a priori, no guarantee that explorations and investigations, with all of the hesitations, uncertainties, and incomprehension they produce, will end each time with an attachment of goods and agencies. When Séguéla invites Sarkozy and Bruni, there is no way of knowing in advance whether they will leave together when the last
digestif

has been drunk or at least leave having exchanged cell phone numbers. All that is known is that Séguéla has skill and many trump cards in hand. The same goes in market agencements and commercial transactions. There is always a risk that no deal will be concluded. The same problem has been appearing for so long, however, that people have learned to put together solutions that produce acceptable results, year in, year out. Social technologies have been designed, tested, and transformed so as to favor successful attachments. They are embodied in know-how, recipes, procedures, and tools that get the job done. The mystery will never be dissipated. No one knows or will ever know the answer to the enigma of the market, because no definitive answer exists. Solutions are constantly being reinvented. What we have, then, are devices imagined and cobbled together that work. It is time to examine some of them.
在离开本节之前，再说最后一点。事先无法保证，探索与探究——连同它们所产生的种种犹疑、不确定与不理解——每次都会导向物品与能动者的附着。当塞格拉邀请萨科齐与布吕尼时，事先无法知道，在最后一杯
餐后酒

喝完之后，他们是否会一起离开，或者至少是在交换了手机号码之后离开。人们所知道的只是：塞格拉有本事，手里握有许多王牌。市场装配与商业交易中也是如此。交易未能达成的风险始终存在。然而，这一问题反复出现已经如此之久，以致人们学会了拼凑出一些解决方案，年复一年地产生可以接受的结果。社会技术被设计、被检验、被改造，以促成成功的附着。它们体现在种种诀窍、配方、程序与工具之中，靠这些把事情办成。这一奥秘永远不会被驱散。没有人知道、也永远不会有人知道市场之谜的答案，因为并不存在最终的答案。解决方案在不断被重新发明。于是，我们所拥有的，是一些被想象出来、被拼凑起来并且管用的装置。现在该来考察其中的一些了。
THREE ATTACHMENT DEVICES FOR ENGAGING GOODS
三种让物品参与其中的附着装置
I am going to suggest that we programmatically distinguish three types of attachment devices: devices for
listening and dialoguing
, devices for
coproducing
, and devices for
addicting

. The importance of the goods in the attachment process and the way they participate in it vary from one family to the other. Listening devices leave little room for goods, which are present only as a backdrop. They provide the dialogue with a few of the references required to make sense of what’s happening on a theatrical stage. These devices aim at convincing potential customers that the good on offer corresponds precisely to what they want and expect and that they should therefore attach themselves to it. With coproduction devices, consumers are involved in the design and production of the goods that are destined for them. These devices put the agents in direct contact with the good and favor attachment because they organize interactions and mutual adaptations: “This good is for you, since you designed it.” With addiction devices, things are endowed with maximal hold on agents’ bodies. In this family of devices, goods are designed to create dependency (or rather a certain degree of dependency), which dissuades agents from freeing themselves and thus quasi-mechanically ensures attachment.
我打算在分析上区分三类附着装置：
倾听与对话
装置、
共同生产
装置，以及
致瘾

装置。物品在附着过程中的重要性，以及它参与这一过程的方式，因装置家族的不同而不同。倾听装置几乎不给物品留出位置，物品仅仅作为背景在场。它们为对话提供若干参照，而这些参照是理解戏剧舞台上所发生之事所必需的。这类装置旨在说服潜在顾客：所供之物恰恰符合他们之所欲、之所期待，因此他们应当附着于它。就共同生产装置而言，消费者被卷入专为他们而设的物品的设计与生产之中。这类装置使行动者与物品直接接触，并促进附着，因为它们组织互动与相互调适：“这件物品是给你的，因为是你设计了它。”就致瘾装置而言，物被赋予对行动者身体的最大掌控力。在这一装置家族中，物品被设计用来制造依赖（或者更确切地说，某种程度的依赖），这种依赖打消行动者摆脱它的念头，从而近乎机械地确保附着。

In practice, attachment devices are a combination of all three types. Successful attachment requires that an agent somehow recognize that what is being offered corresponds to what they want. An agreement can be obtained, however, only if the consumers were involved at some point in the good’s design process, either directly or indirectly. Finally, to prevent the attachment from dissipating before the transaction takes place means establishing a certain dependency with bodies and minds. In the following, I will give a stylized description of these three families of devices, with a few examples to show how they function. I will then briefly discuss the detachment mechanisms without which no market transaction would be conceivable. Sellers must also go through a transformation and accept being detached from goods in which they have invested themselves.

在实践中，附着装置是三种类型的组合。成功的附着要求行动者以某种方式认识到：所提供之物符合他们之所欲。然而，只有消费者在某个时刻——无论是直接还是间接——参与了物品的设计过程，协议才可能达成。最后，要防止附着在交易发生之前消散，就意味着要与身体和心智建立某种依赖。下文我将对这三个装置家族作一番程式化的描述，并举几个例子说明它们如何运作。随后我会简要讨论脱离机制——没有这些机制，任何市场交易都无从设想。卖方同样必须经历一次转化，接受从自己曾倾注心力的物品中脱离出来。
DIALOGUE: HERE’S WHAT YOU NEED!

For the seller, the simplest way to begin the attachment process is to convince potential consumers that the good on offer corresponds exactly to what they need, that it brings an answer to the problems they have or should have.
对话：这就是您需要的！
对卖方而言，启动附着过程最简单的方式，就是说服潜在消费者：所供之物恰恰符合他们之所需，能够为他们已经面临或本该面临的问题提供答案。

The function of this type of device is to gradually ascertain what customers expect, hope for, or want by getting them to articulate it themselves. To reach that point, the conversation takes the form of a dialogue similar to the
chjam’è rispondi

Corsican songs, which take the form of a succession of improvised questions and answers. If the dialogue is properly directed, and if all goes well, it can lead to an agreement (“Here is what you need” answered by a “Yes, this is the good I want”) and to the promise of a successful attachment.
这类装置的功能，是让顾客自己把话说出来，从而逐步弄清他们期待什么、希望什么、想要什么。为达到这一点，交谈采取对话的形式，类似于科西嘉岛的“
chjam’è rispondi
”歌曲——那是一连串即兴的提问与回答。如果对话得到恰当的引导，如果一切顺利，它就能导向一项协议（“这就是您需要的”，对方答以“是的，这正是我想要的物品”），并导向成功附着的允诺。

The simplest way to get a customer to recognize that he really wants the good on offer is to organize a face-to-face meeting between the seller and the customer. They can then enter into dialogue. Whether a grocer, butcher, hardware vendor, or salesman who travels abroad, any seller will tell you that learning to manage this type of conversation, both with regular customers and with newcomers, is essential to success. The conversation is sustained by the presence of goods. Laid out in the stall or appearing in the form of catalogs, flyers, or videos, they are available to be appreciated, scrutinized, or touched. At any moment, when reticence surfaces or an objection appears, returning to the goods can help overcome the difficulty and allow the attachment to progress.

要让顾客承认他确实想要所供之物，最简单的办法是安排卖方与顾客面对面会面。他们于是可以进入对话。无论是杂货商、肉贩、五金商，还是远赴海外推销的销售员，任何卖方都会告诉你：学会驾驭这类交谈——无论对象是老主顾还是新来者——是成功的关键。交谈因物品的在场而得以维持。物品陈列在摊位上，或以商品目录、传单、视频的形式出现，可供人欣赏、端详或触摸。任何时候，一旦迟疑浮现或异议出现，回到物品那里就有助于克服困难，让附着继续推进。

Pitchers are masters of this art, which is as difficult as it is ancient. In his work on very small and medium companies, sociologist Alexandre Mallard tells the story of how a vendor crisscrossing the countryside in his van in the Vendée understood there was no point in waiting for customers in the marketplace.

He tracks them down at home, one by one. Two honks on the horn announce his arrival. “It’s me, it’s you, I am coming for you, Madame! Look at this fish, it’s your favorite. I am at your service, here to help, here to solve your problems.” The conversation continues from one visit to the next, always like the
chjam’è rispondi

, chiming and responding. Such a conversation, in which the seller, the customer, and the merchandise meet in the flesh, can also be adapted to industry. Sociologist Liz McFall makes this point when she tells the story of the life insurance market in the UK. As she recounts, experienced agents had to be sent to each home to present the product while being attentive to suspicious clients. The agents succeeded beyond the industry’s wildest expectations. They became intimate friends, confidants, for this mass of poor people, renewing limited-time contracts week after week — not an isolated pitcher, but hundreds of salesmen in dialogue with a multitude of customers treated as unique people.
叫卖者（pitcher，即擅长吆喝推销之人）是这门艺术的大师，而这门艺术既古老又艰难。社会学家亚历山大·马拉尔（Alexandre Mallard）在研究微型与中型企业时，讲述了这样一位商人的故事：他开着厢式货车在旺代（Vendée）乡间穿梭，明白在集市上等顾客是没有意义的。
他逐个上门找他们。两声喇叭宣告他的到来。“是我呀，是您呀，我找您来了，夫人！瞧这条鱼，是您最爱吃的。我为您效劳，来帮您，来替您解决问题。”交谈从一次拜访延续到下一次，始终像
chjam’è rispondi

那样，一唱一和，此呼彼应。这样一场交谈——卖方、顾客与商品亲身相遇——也可以推广到其他产业中。社会学家莉兹·麦克福尔（Liz McFall）在讲述英国寿险市场的故事时正指出了这一点。据她叙述，必须派有经验的代理人挨家挨户登门介绍产品，同时留意那些心存疑虑的客户。代理人的成功超出了业界最狂野的期望。他们成了这一大群穷人亲密的朋友、知心人，一周又一周地续签限期合同——不是一个孤零零的叫卖者，而是数百名销售员，与众多被当作独特个人来对待的顾客对话。

The internet is a great, low-cost platform for launching and keeping up these personalized conversations in which customers on a large scale make explicit what they expect and appreciate. Sociologist Kevin Mellet identifies three strategies. The first turns to the internet as a vector for contagion to create buzz. The second seeks to reach and convince opinion leaders or prescribers who will come to act as relays and spread the exchanges to their followers. Finally, the third strategy is to use tools such as Facebook to animate the network of those who declare themselves as your friends, starting a “real” dialogue with them, without intermediaries.

互联网是一个绝佳的低成本平台，可用来发起并维持这类个性化交谈，让顾客大规模地明说自己期待什么、欣赏什么。社会学家凯文·梅莱（Kevin Mellet）识别出三种策略。第一种把互联网当作传染载体，以制造话题热度。第二种设法触及并说服意见领袖或推介者，让他们充当转播者，把交流传播给自己的追随者。最后，第三种策略是利用 Facebook 之类的工具，激活那些自称是你朋友的人所组成的网络，与他们——不经任何中介——展开“真正的”对话。
These strategies participate in a more general movement toward research on consumers, their practices, their aspirations, or their problems.

This research is not disinterested. It aims to convey consumers’ diverse and sometimes contradictory words to companies; it is led by a myriad of players who try to make the customers speak so as to better capture them. Many complementary methods are used, including statistical analysis (for instance, using data related to socioprofessional categories), collecting the data picked up by the sales force, face-to-face interviews with customers, and in situ observation of practices, focus groups, or neighborhood meetings where products are displayed for comment. Anything goes. There is no limit on the imagination. These investigations allow for endless back-and-forth. They establish not one, but several truths, all temporary and changing. They play a central role in the design of advertising campaigns, in the conversations they feed and that feed them.
这些策略参与了一场更为普遍的运动：对消费者及其实践、渴望或问题的研究。

这项研究绝非无私之举。它的目的是把消费者多样、有时彼此矛盾的话语传达给企业；它由形形色色的参与者主导，这些人设法让顾客开口，以便更好地俘获他们。研究运用许多互补的方法，包括统计分析（例如使用与社会职业类别相关的数据）、收集销售队伍采集的数据、与顾客面对面访谈、对实践的现场观察、焦点小组，以及展示产品以供评论的社区会议。一切手段皆可，想象力没有界限。这些调查允许无休止的往复。它们确立的不是一种真理，而是好几种真理，全都是暂时的、变动不居的。它们在广告活动的设计中、在它们所滋养又反过来滋养它们的对话中，扮演着核心角色。

Research on consumers does not lose sight of the goods themselves. It implicates these goods in the conversation to varying degrees. In the food industry, there are tastings; in showrooms, real consumers are invited to see, touch, smell, react, say, and thus give a live commentary on the force of their attachments. Success, however, is not guaranteed. Before they are definitively certified and measured by the flow of money, there is something uncertain and fragile about attachments.
对消费者的研究并未忽视物品本身。它让这些物品不同程度地卷入交谈。食品业有试吃；在陈列室里，真实消费者受邀去看、去摸、去闻、去反应、去言说，从而对自身附着的强度作出当场评述。然而，成功并无保证。在附着被货币流最终确认并度量之前，它总带着某种不确定与脆弱。

The reversible, temporary, and partial nature of attachments is not necessarily a flaw. Of course, one needs attached consumers, but they should not be too attached, otherwise markets would fall into repetitive routines and would soon fall asleep for good. What matters is that the conversation not falter. A conversation requires upkeep. One has to rekindle the relation to the consumer, honk twice, begin research afresh. For instance, loyalty cards make this possible by maintaining contact and updating the data.
附着具有可逆、暂时和局部的性质，这未必是缺陷。当然，人们需要已附着的消费者，但他们不应附着过深，否则市场就会陷入重复的常规，很快一睡不醒。要紧的是对话不至于中断。对话需要维护。必须重新点燃与消费者的关系，再按两声喇叭，重新开始研究。例如，会员卡通过保持联系、更新数据，使这一点成为可能。

As both McFall and Mallard show, keeping up a conversation from the supply side, or actually, several parallel conversations, requires a great deal of energy and resources. It requires an impeccable organization, one capable of mobilizing multitudes of experts and professionals inside and outside the company, sometimes in real time, in order to coordinate, process the data, and brief agents sent out “on the ground.” In his work on call centers, Mallard observes that even if conversations are carefully prepared and framed, they sometimes slip out of control because the profiling of the interlocutors and their matching have not been well adjusted or because the organization of the conversations suffers from a poor allocation of resources, which increases the waiting time before the conversation begins.

正如麦克福尔与马拉尔所表明的，从供给侧维持一场对话——实际上是维持若干场并行的对话——需要大量精力与资源。它需要无可挑剔的组织，能够调动公司内外大批专家与专业人士，有时还要实时运作，以便协调、处理数据，并向派往“一线”的代理人作简报。马拉尔在研究呼叫中心时观察到：即便对话经过精心准备与框定，它们有时仍会失控，原因要么是对话者的画像与匹配调整不当，要么是对话的组织在资源分配上存在缺陷，以致对话开始前的等待时间被拉长。

Those who design and put goods on offer must also be prepared to detach from them. Of course, there is no ambiguity. All of the protagonists know that this exchange of words will conclude with a commercial transaction. It is thus an interesting conversation, and it is not easy to manage, especially when the entire organization needs to be taught how to begin a dialogue that has no other purpose than to attach,
to get
, the customer.

Offering help, showing attention or empathy, without forgetting that one is there to further commerce is indeed something that has to be learned. There are theater classes that teach the skill. Mallard describes how, over the course of a telephone conversation between a customer and the employee of a call center, the latter alternates with mastery between personalized speaking and exchanges that show that there are two roles, that of the seller and that of the customer. (In one moment, “My name is Dominique. How can I help you?” In the next, “Orange reminds you, dear Mr. Callon, that your cable contract cannot be terminated free of charge before the end of November.”)

This role playing can go awry at any point. The seller moves ahead on a knife’s edge. Too much familiarity or not enough, and the conversation is off to a bad start. All the more because the customer is on the alert: they know that after a cascade of intermediaries have intervened, they risk being
had
by the discussion, by Dominique or by anonymous slogans or advertisements.
设计并把物品投放市场的人，也必须准备好从中脱离。当然，这里没有含糊之处。所有当事人都知道，这场言语交换将以一笔商业交易收尾。因此这是一场有趣的对话，管理起来并不容易，尤其当整个组织都需要被教会如何去开启一场除了附着、
抓住
顾客之外别无目的的对话时。
提供帮助，表示关心或共情，同时不忘自己到此是为了推进生意——这确实是必须学习的东西。有些戏剧课专门教授这项技能。马拉尔描述了这样一幕：在顾客与呼叫中心员工的一通电话中，后者娴熟地在个性化言说与表明存在两种角色——卖方与顾客——的交流之间交替。（这一刻是“我叫多米尼克。我能为您做什么？”下一刻是“Orange 提醒您，亲爱的卡隆先生，您的有线服务合同在十一月底之前不能免费终止。”）
这种角色扮演随时可能出错。卖方行走在刀锋之上。熟络过头或不够熟络，对话一开始就会走岔。更何况顾客正保持警觉：他们知道，在一连串中介介入之后，自己有可能被这番谈话
耍弄
，被多米尼克耍弄，或被匿名的口号与广告耍弄。
At any moment, the conversation could veer into lies, bad faith, dirty tricks, cynicism, cheating, or fraud. It could also slip into a noncommercial register.

Skillfully navigating between these two pitfalls (developing arguments that could turn out to be fallacious and failing to complete the transaction) requires a great deal of know-how. In such a dialogue, what is at stake is neither the sincerity of the seller nor the credulity of the customer, but effectively framing passions and affects. When the conversation is adroitly steered, no one is fooled, no one believes it, and yet everyone believes it, because everyone knows that an objective, definite truth is out of reach. The French terms put it well — a pitcher is a
bonimenteur
, one who lies well.
Not everyone is up to the job of lying well. It is infinitely more difficult than telling the truth.
对话随时可能滑向谎言、不诚实、卑鄙伎俩、犬儒主义、欺骗或诈伪。它也可能滑入非商业的语域。
要在这两个陷阱之间（一边是提出可能被证明为谬误的论证，一边是无法完成交易）巧妙地穿行，需要高超的诀窍。在这样一场对话中，真正攸关的，既不是卖方的真诚，也不是顾客的轻信，而是有效地框定激情与情动。当对话被巧妙地驾驭时，没有人上当，没有人相信它，然而每个人都相信它，因为大家都知道，客观而确定的真理遥不可及。法文的说法很到位——叫卖者就是
bonimenteur
，即善于说谎的人。
并非人人都能把谎说得好。它比说真话要难上无穷倍。
COPRODUCTION: YOUR TURN!

Conversation cannot be circumvented. Silent relations cannot lead to attachments. However, if conversations are cut off from their object, the goods and things, or if they do not get close enough to them and remain mere verbal exchanges, they fast lose all (commercial) interest and soon ring hollow. Those who design
conversation devices
are keenly aware of this connection. In order to facilitate and reinforce the production of attachments, they contrive to give goods ever more chances to intervene and express themselves.
共同生产：轮到您了！
对话无法绕开。沉默的关系无法导向附着。然而，如果对话与其对象——物品与物——相隔绝，或者如果对话没有充分接近它们，只停留在言语交换，那么它很快就会丧失一切（商业）意义，不久便显得空洞无物。设计
对话装置
的人深知这一关联。为了便利并强化附着的生产，他们设法给物品越来越多的机会介入并表达自身。

What if the goods themselves were the main actors in exchanges? And what better way to manage this than by inviting consumers into the design and production process? The more closely I am associated with the manufacturing of the good that is destined for me and the earlier I can intervene in the discussion around its qualities and its shaping, the greater the chance I will become sincerely and lastingly attached to it in the end.
如果物品本身才是交换的主角，那又会怎样？而要处理这一点，还有什么比邀请消费者进入设计与生产过程更好的办法？那件专为我而造的物品，其制造过程与我关联得越紧密，我越早介入围绕其品质与成形而展开的讨论，我最终真诚而持久地附着于它的机会就越大。

The organization of innovation processes attests to the efficiency of devices that aim to involve customers in the innovation process to ensure success. Eric von Hippel calls this the “democratization of innovation,” underscoring that the design of new products is opening up.

Although the term “democratization” may be excessive, since access to design processes remains very selective, it does point to the increasing involvement of users. Exposure to goods helps those for whom they are intended learn what they want. For instance, in the case of therapy development, involving patient groups to attach to the treatments and molecules they have helped test is a phenomenon that will not disappear anytime soon. Sociologist Vololona Rabeharisoa cites the example of a small group of patients suffering from an extremely rare blood disease who work in close contact with a few researchers and doctors to test a promising substance.

Likewise, in their history of treatments against cancer, STS scholars Alberto Cambrosio and Peter Keating document how patients are involved in intermediary decisions (such as whether to continue the trial or not) and are thereby led, little by little, to become dependent upon the very treatments they are helping develop.
Countless studies show that this type of organization is spreading, notably in the service sector. New concepts are invented to describe it. There is talk of a new regime of innovation
or of the
prosumer
and of
consomma(c)tion
, two neologisms that contract the two words “consumer” and “producer.” Management scientist Henry Chesbrough successfully introduced the notion of
openness
, pointing to the multiple agents liable to be involved in the design and production of new products.

It would in fact be more precise to speak of the openness of products themselves: over the course of their qualification, they are profiled in such a way as to solicit reactions from a wide range of relevant agents.
创新过程的组织，证明了那些旨在让顾客参与创新过程以确保成功的装置何等有效。埃里克·冯·希佩尔（Eric von Hippel）称之为“创新的民主化”（democratization of innovation），强调新产品的设计正在开放。

尽管“民主化”一词或许言过其实——因为进入设计过程的机会仍然极具选择性——它确实指向用户日益加深的参与。接触物品，有助于那些物品所指向的人弄清自己想要什么。例如，在疗法开发中，让患者团体参与进来，使他们附着于自己曾帮助测试的治疗方案与分子，这一现象短期内不会消失。社会学家沃洛洛娜·拉贝阿里索阿（Vololona Rabeharisoa）举了一个例子：一小群罹患一种极其罕见血液病的患者，与少数研究者、医生密切合作，测试一种有前景的物质。
同样，科学技术研究（STS）学者阿尔贝托·坎布罗西奥（Alberto Cambrosio）与彼得·基廷（Peter Keating）在他们关于癌症治疗史的研究中，记录了患者如何被卷入中间决策（例如是否继续试验），并由此一点一点地变得依赖于他们正在帮助开发的疗法本身。
无数研究表明，这类组织正在扩散，尤其是在服务业。人们发明新概念来描述它。有人谈论新的创新体制，
也有人谈论产消者（
prosumer
）与消费行动（
consomma(c)tion
）——这两个新词把“消费者”（consumer）与“生产者”（producer）两词缩合在一起。管理学家亨利·切斯布鲁（Henry Chesbrough）成功引入了
开放性
的概念，指出可能有多种行动者参与新产品的设计与生产。
事实上，更准确的说法是产品本身的开放性：在品质界定的过程中，产品被塑造成能够引出各类相关行动者的反应。

According to art historian Svetlana Alpers, Rembrandt anticipated this movement. In an attempt to live from his art and rid himself of his patrons’ influence, he undertook to build a market for his work.

Not only was Rembrandt an entrepreneur, making his studio into a production unit and his students into collaborators committed to a collective project, he also imagined a series of innovative setups, singularizing transactions even as he increased their number. Each painting that left the studio was extended in the form of new works, each original, but slightly different from the previous ones, notably through a detail or two discussed with the patrons. Art historians have referred to these as “multiple originals.” Furthermore, his paintings had ongoing careers. Rembrandt retained the right to recall a painting, if necessary through repurchasing, in order to touch it up. Numerous notarized documents specify how touch-ups were decided and carried out. A painting was not a unique accomplishment, frozen for all of time. For instance, even as it was being produced,
The Conspiracy of Claudius Civilis

was conceived of as a work in progress, the first of a long series of variations and transformations in which those who successively acquired the painting would be involved. Through a process of extreme singularization and carefully maintained openness, the paintings were thus transformed into so many open-ended sites of creation. Amateurs and clients were invited to these sites, and as they participated at some stage in the qualification of the painting, they became attached to it. As commercial passiva(c)tion dictates, it remained only for Rembrandt to ensure that this evolving work would be attributed to him. He did this with consummate mastery. As Alpers explains, Rembrandt was “an entrepreneur of the self.”
艺术史家斯维特兰娜·阿尔珀斯（Svetlana Alpers）认为，伦勃朗（Rembrandt）预见了这一运动。为了靠自己的艺术为生，并摆脱赞助人的影响，他着手为自己的作品建立一个市场。

伦勃朗不仅是一位企业家，把画室变成生产单位，把学生变成投身于一项集体项目的合作者；他还设想了一系列创新性的设置，在增加交易数量的同时使每一笔交易独一化。每一幅离开画室的画作，都以新作品的形式得到延展，每幅都是原作，却与前一幅略有不同，尤其是通过一两处与赞助人商议过的细节。艺术史家称之为“多重原作”（multiple originals）。此外，他的画作有着持续的生命。伦勃朗保留召回一幅画作的权利，必要时通过回购，以便对它加以修改。大量公证文件具体说明了修改如何决定、如何执行。一幅画并非一件凝固于永恒之中的独一成就。例如，《克劳狄乌斯·西维利斯的阴谋》（
The Conspiracy of Claudius Civilis

）在创作过程中就被设想为一件进行中的作品，是一长串变体与转化中的第一件，而先后购得这幅画的人都将参与其中。通过极端的独一化与精心维持的开放性，这些画作于是变成了一个个开放的创作场所。爱好者与主顾受邀来到这些场所，由于他们在某个阶段参与了画作的品质界定，他们便附着于它。正如商业被动化所要求的那样，伦勃朗只需确保这件不断演化的作品被归之于他。他以炉火纯青的技艺做到了这一点。正如阿尔珀斯所解释的，伦勃朗是“自我的企业家”。

Openness is increasingly becoming a crucial quality of goods. It is a powerful force of affectation and attachment in that it goes so far as to include, often explicitly, the possibility or even the necessity of adaptations and requalifications after the commercial transaction has been completed. Tinkerers prefer materials that allow them to improvise and to . . . tinker; similarly, it seems that the most dedicated coders clamor to praise Linux, Android, Firefox, and all the open systems and software, rather than Apple and its locked systems. In an excellent self-analysis, management scientist Hans Kjellberg convincingly documented how a “collector’s item” car (by definition open to requalification), once acquired, and even as it is itself transformed, entered his life, transforming his relations with those close to him, his friends, and his children, redefining his modes of life.
The transfer of property, the crucial moment of attachment, reinforces itself. The thing
has
the consumer as much as the consumer
has
the thing.

开放性正日益成为物品的一项关键品质。它是一种强大的感发与附着之力，因为它甚至常常明确地包含这种可能，乃至这种必要：在商业交易完成之后对物品加以调适与重新界定品质。修补匠偏爱那些让他们得以即兴发挥、得以……修修补补的材料；同样，似乎最投入的程序员也争相赞美 Linux、Android、Firefox 以及所有开放的系统与软件，而不是苹果及其封闭系统。管理学家汉斯·谢尔贝里（Hans Kjellberg）在一篇出色的自我分析中令人信服地记录了一辆“收藏品”（collector’s item）汽车（按定义即对重新界定品质保持开放）如何在他购得之后、甚至在它自身被转化的同时，进入他的生活，改变他与亲人、朋友和子女的关系，重新界定他的生活方式。
财产转移——附着的关键时刻——自我强化。物
占有
消费者，正如消费者
占有
物。
Marketing has not failed to notice the development of openness.
It has multiplied ways of soliciting consumers, leading them to interact more directly with goods and opening the possibilities of requalification.
营销界并未忽视开放性的发展。
它倍增了招引消费者的方式，引导他们与物品更直接地互动，并开启了重新界定品质的可能性。
The simplest, most rudimentary mechanism is the invention of self-service retail spaces, which organize a face-off between consumers and products.

As Cochoy has amply demonstrated, this arrangement sets up a consumer who has no choice but to be forced to choose for himself. The consumer is constituted as a “free” subject (a freedom that is, of course, highly constrained), who, like any free subject, hesitates and formulates questions for himself, but eventually reaches a decision to which and through which he feels committed. This is not a matter of a simple conversation of self with self. In other words, it is still a conversation between self and the professionals who have organized the presentation of the goods. Tailored with inscriptions and messages, the products on the shelf, and indeed the shelving itself, speak to the consumer, attract attention, suggest further investigations and explorations: the products are loquacious, expressive through the simple fact of being there, squeezed up against one another, collected and selected. As the consumer passes in front of the shelves, the framings change, alternating and blending into each other; the shopping cart, a crucial invention, operates as a form of memory, displaying what has been chosen and perhaps leading the consumer to reconsider the choices in front of their eyes. Things hail the consumer, forcing the consumer to take them into account.
最简单、最原始的机制，是自助零售空间的发明，它组织了消费者与产品之间的对峙。

正如科舒瓦（Cochoy）充分论证的，这一安排建构起一个别无选择、只能被迫为自己作选择的消费者。消费者被建构为“自由”主体（这种自由当然受到高度约束）；他像任何自由主体一样犹豫、向自己提出问题，但最终作出一个决定，并且感到自己投入其中、与之绑在一起。这并非简单的自我与自我的对话。换句话说，它仍然是自我与那些组织物品呈现的专业人士之间的对话。货架上的产品，乃至货架本身，都配以铭写与讯息，向消费者言说，吸引注意，提示进一步的探查与探索：产品是饶舌的，仅凭它们在那里、彼此挤靠、被收集与被挑选这一事实，就富有表达力。当消费者从货架前经过，框定不断变化，交替并彼此融合；购物车——一项关键发明——作为一种记忆形式运作，展示已经选中的东西，或许还引导消费者重新考虑眼前的选择。物向消费者发出召唤，迫使消费者把它们纳入考量。

The brand phenomenon has allowed marketing to go much further in putting the consumer to work. Take the case of American Apparel and the campaign it launched in the 1990s to establish its place in the clothing market, as analyzed by sociologist Carolin Gerlitz. The brand created its style.

Its first step was to approach customers, inquiring into their behavior. American Apparel’s gamble was to enter into people’s intimate sphere. The company launched a campaign of photographs that closed in on the body, scrutinizing faults, beads of sweat, or burgeoning cellulite and unhesitatingly evoking sexuality. By defending a different exploration, American Apparel distinguished itself from its competitors, which distanced themselves from real bodies and dissimulated what they considered imperfections, making pants float and showing the flaps of checkered shirts flying in the wind. The brand stuck to the body with clothes that stuck to the skin, showing, rather than coating —figure-fitting clothing made from supple and elastic material. It established the terms of an original conversation that would take place with things: T-shirts, shirts, tights, and pants, these are the things that speak and are spoken of. It might have failed, yet it succeeded. A certain identity emerged in contrast to existing identities, with its own social spaces and urban sites, such as East London. The brand and its aesthetic were anchored in groups whose identities it helped forge. Meanwhile, and this is what is interesting, the American Apparel style progressively became a tool for participatory creation. In fact, users spontaneously associated certain practices with the brand, although the brand did nothing to fashion them. (This universe can be explored by searching the web with “American Apparel” as the keyword.) Ideas, identities, quirky and different practices were connected as though the brand had become a platform. It became a common noun that designated a way of being and dressing, stimulating imaginations and suggestions that then needed only to be collated. Not only did the conversation around the existing goods offered by the company spread; what is more, there emerged from all sides novel associations likely to lead to new products. The brand became an arrangement for participatory creation, putting a vast number of agents to work on a volunteer basis. In some cases, a machine such as this one can become extremely productive. Gerlitz cites the example of Dove, which mobilized a whole range of intervening parties, putting groups of women to work by organizing forums and sites and orchestrating a vast movement around the questioning of beauty norms, especially those spread by the media. The brand thus managed to take part in the elaboration of new practices and new meanings around beauty. After such collective and highly mediatized work, which resembles a social movement, consumers are all the more likely to become attached, since the good is itself attached to the new practices, stakes, and preoccupations that they share. The product has been opened, unfolded; it has been enriched, transformed, inserted into a new network of associations. All of this is accomplished by the brand, which is to marketing what collaborative platforms are to new product design. The brand attaches, and one becomes attached to it. It becomes a collective force that performs the opening of goods and pushes them into maximal entwinement with ethical, political, or cultural preoccupations, which it in turn transforms. It is not (only), as has so often been said, a device for producing trust. To echo Gerlitz, the brand manages value flows from opposite directions. As the good becomes multivalent, its economic value increases.
品牌现象使营销得以在让消费者投入工作方面走得更远。以 American Apparel 为例，以及它在 1990 年代为在服装市场中确立地位而发起的广告活动——社会学家卡罗琳·格尔利茨（Carolin Gerlitz）对此作了分析。这个品牌创造了自身的风格。

它的第一步是接近顾客，探询他们的行为。American Apparel 的赌注，是进入人们的私密领域。公司发起了一场摄影活动，镜头逼近身体，细察瑕疵、汗珠或初现的橘皮组织，并毫不犹豫地唤起性。通过捍卫一种不同的探索，American Apparel 把自己与竞争者区分开来——后者与真实身体保持距离，掩饰它们眼中的不完美，让长裤悬浮空中，让格纹衬衫的衣角在风中飘扬。这个品牌让衣物紧贴身体，紧贴皮肤，不是遮盖而是展示——即以柔软而有弹性的材料制成贴身衣物。它为一场将与物一同展开的原创对话确立了条件：T 恤、衬衫、连裤袜与长裤，这些物既在言说，也被谈论。它本可能失败，却成功了。某种身份在与既有身份的对照中浮现出来，拥有自己的社会空间与城市场所，例如东伦敦。品牌及其美学锚定于一些群体之中，并帮助塑造了这些群体的身份。与此同时——这一点才是有趣之处——American Apparel 的风格逐渐成为一种参与式创造的工具。事实上，用户自发地把某些实践与这个品牌联系起来，尽管品牌并未为此做过什么。（只要以“American Apparel”为关键词在网上搜索，便可探索这个宇宙。）观念、身份、古怪而另类的实践被连接起来，仿佛品牌已经成为一个平台。它变成了一个普通名词，指称一种存在与穿着的方式，激发想象，催生种种建议，而这些东西随后只需被汇集起来。不仅围绕公司现有物品的对话扩散开来；更有甚者，新的联结从四面八方涌现，可能导向新产品。品牌变成了一种参与式创造的装配，让大量行动者自愿投入工作。在某些情况下，这样一台机器可以变得极具生产力。格尔利茨举了多芬（Dove）的例子：它调动了一整系列介入者，通过组织论坛与网站，把一群群女性投入工作，围绕对美之规范的质疑——尤其是媒体所传播的那些规范——编排了一场浩大的运动。品牌于是得以参与围绕美的新实践与新意义的建构。在这样一场集体性的、高度媒介化、类似社会运动的工作之后，消费者更有可能附着，因为物品本身也附着于他们所共享的新实践、新利害与新关切。产品被打开了、展开了；它被充实、被转化，被插入一个新的联结网络。这一切都由品牌完成；品牌之于营销，正如协作平台之于新产品设计。品牌使他人附着，人们也附着于品牌。它成为一种使物品开放起来的集体力量，把物品推入与伦理、政治或文化关切的极致缠绕，而这些关切又反过来被它转化。它并不（只）像人们常说的那样，是一台生产信任的装置。呼应格尔利茨的说法，品牌管理着来自相反方向的价值流。随着物品承载的价值面向增多，其经济价值随之上升。
ADDICTION: PAY TO GET EVEN MORE ATTACHED!

Starting and maintaining a dialogue is good. It is even better to orient the dialogue toward the codesign and coproduction of goods, which provides those for whom they are destined with margins of maneuver to experience and express what they want. As the affectation process proceeds from one device to another, things weigh more and more. But the most effective approach for attaching people is to manage the dialogue so that goods condition behavior directly, become indispensable to the customers, and throw them into a state of dependence that they cannot dream of leaving.
致瘾：付钱，好让自己附着得更深！
开启并维持对话是好的。把对话引向物品的共同设计与共同生产则更好，因为这为物品所指向的人提供了回旋余地，去体验并表达他们想要什么。随着感发过程从一个装置推进到另一个装置，物的分量也越来越重。但要把人附着住，最有效的办法是驾驭对话，使物品直接制约行为，成为顾客不可或缺之物，并把他们抛入一种他们做梦也想不到要离开的依赖状态。

Devices that seek to addict the user are not new. In their unnerving simplicity, they are sometimes stunningly efficient. A few years ago, Lucky Strike put cigarettes on the market with a mentholated tablet in the filter. When the tablet heated up and the smoker pressed the “on” button, the taste of the cigarette changed. Apparently, adolescents loved them. To use their expression, they would “blow the tab” as fast as possible. This little device had two effects. The first was to bring a taste that had been ascertained to bring a pleasant sensation to the young smoker, inciting him to breathe in deeply. To swallow smoke so young is to take a serious step toward long-term addiction and also, as a possible secondary effect, lung cancer. Inciting the adolescent to “blow the tab” is a more secure and radical commercial strategy of attachment than all the slogans and advertisements put together.

设法让使用者致瘾的装置并不新鲜。它们以令人不安的简单性，有时达到惊人的效率。几年前，好彩（Lucky Strike）把过滤嘴中带有薄荷丸的香烟投放市场。当薄荷丸受热、吸烟者按下“开启”按钮时，香烟的味道便发生变化。据说青少年很喜欢。用他们的话说，他们会尽快“把珠子爆开”。这个小装置有两个效果。第一，把一种经确认能带来愉悦感觉的味道送给年轻吸烟者，诱使他深深吸入。年纪轻轻就吞下烟雾，是朝着长期成瘾迈出的严重一步，而且还可能带来一个附带后果：肺癌。诱使青少年“把珠子爆开”，是一种比所有口号与广告加起来都更可靠、更彻底的商业附着策略。

In order to understand the mechanisms of addiction as the same mechanisms that attach users to goods (defined in this model of markets as having completed the decisive step toward establishing a bilateral transaction with consent to pay), let us return to Las Vegas with anthropologist Natasha Schüll.

In Nevada, gambling has become a full-blown economic and commercial activity with an industrial organization that is exclusively and massively oriented toward the production of addictive behavior and the accumulation of the immense commercial benefits it produces. To explain this economic success, it would be too easy to appeal to
panem et circenses

(bread and games), a human nature that needs to have its guilty weaknesses flattered. Turning to such an explanation would seriously underestimate the colossal investments in brain power and in dollars required to actualize these inclinations and to transform more and more occasional gamblers in search of distraction into dependent, immersed, drowned gamblers who seek only to cut themselves off from the world around them. So much research and experimentation is necessary to organize this dependency and to ensure that it brings maximum profits to the casino that reducing addiction to a face-offbetween a solo gambler and a screen is blindness. In silent conversation with this gambler are machines, high-tech innovations, armies of architects, psychologists, and marketers, other casinos competing for the most competitive algorithms, mathematicians aiming to establish the laws of chance so that it really is true chance (which is not as easy as it seems), battalions of lawyers and elected officials debating the morality or lack thereof of such practices, and governments eagerly amassing the taxes flowing into state coffers.
为了把致瘾机制理解为使用户附着于物品的同一套机制（在这个市场模型中，附着被界定为：已经迈出决定性的一步，朝着在同意支付的基础上建立双边交易推进），让我们随人类学家娜塔莎·舒尔（Natasha Schüll）回到拉斯维加斯。
在内华达，赌博已成为一项充分发育的经济与商业活动，其产业组织专一地、大规模地朝向致瘾行为的生产，以及这种行为所产生的巨额商业利益的积累。要解释这一经济成功，诉诸“面包与马戏”（
panem et circenses

，面包与娱乐）——一种必须让其有罪的弱点得到奉承的人性——未免太容易了。求诸这样的解释，会严重低估为使这些倾向成为现实、为把越来越多寻找消遣的偶尔赌徒转化为依赖的、沉浸的、沉溺的赌徒——他们只想把自己与周围世界隔绝开来——所需的脑力与美元的巨额投入。组织这种依赖，并确保它为赌场带来最大利润，需要如此多的研究与实验，因此把成瘾化约为单个赌徒与屏幕之间的对峙，纯属盲目。与这个赌徒进行无声对话的，是机器、高科技创新、成群的建筑师、心理学家与营销人员，是争夺最具竞争力算法的其他赌场，是试图确立偶然性法则、使偶然真正成为偶然（这并不像看上去那么容易）的数学家，是辩论此类实践有德与否的成批律师与民选官员，是急于征收流入国库之税款的政府。

Schüll describes the design and functioning of these addiction devices with surgical precision. First, a long, labyrinthine path attracts the customer to Las Vegas (low-cost plane tickets, price-reduced hotel rooms) and leads him without much thought to the heart of the casino, into what gamblers call the “zone,” a closed space of a few square feet, an island in the ocean of the some hundred thousand square feet of the gaming room where all of the variables (temperature, light, colors, sounds, and smells) have been calculated and tested to provoke emotion. The gambler is then facing
his

machine, designed to take the measure of their propensity for addictive practices and, if possible, to reinforce them. The goal is to increase the speed of bets, to not interrupt the gambler while he is winning (so he continues to place the winnings), to avoid wasting the gambler’s time cashing in on his gains or searching for more money (for instance, by transforming credit cards into betting instruments), to settle him for as long as possible — he must leave his seat only to satisfy physiological needs such as to go to the toilet or to eat. Everything is controlled: what one hears (integrating background noise), what one sees, what one feels. Comfort is curated in the smallest details, such as those seats, which subtly vibrate depending on what is happening. If attachment and addiction are successful, it is because the service is designed with the active participation of consumers through the dialogue and coproduction practices the casinos have set up. The machines are an environment in and of themselves; they capture gamblers emotionally and retain them.
舒尔以外科手术般的精确，描述了这些致瘾装置的设计与运作。首先，一条漫长而迷宫般的路径把顾客吸引到拉斯维加斯（低价机票、降价酒店房间），并让他不加多想地走进赌场核心，进入赌徒所谓的“区域”（zone）——一个只有几平方英尺的封闭空间，是约十万平方英尺赌场大厅这片海洋中的一座孤岛；在那里，所有变量（温度、光线、色彩、声音与气味）都经过计算与测试，以激发情绪。赌徒于是面对
自己的

机器；机器被设计用来测量其从事致瘾实践的倾向，并在可能时强化这种倾向。目标是提高下注速度，在赌徒赢钱时不打断他（好让他继续把赢来的钱押上去），避免浪费赌徒兑现收益或寻找更多钱的时间（例如把信用卡变成下注工具），让他尽可能久地安坐——只有为了满足上厕所或进食之类的生理需要，他才离开座位。一切都受到控制：听到什么（把背景噪音整合进来）、看到什么、感觉到什么。舒适被精心打理到最细微之处，例如那些随所发生之事微微震动的座椅。如果说附着与致瘾成功了，那是因为服务是在消费者通过赌场设置的对话与共同生产实践积极参与之下设计出来的。机器本身就是一种环境；它们在情感上俘获赌徒，并把他们留住。

In great detail, Schüll shows how essential elements of affectation are integrated into the slot machine’s software and its microprocessors. For example, the reels give the impression they are set off by the push of a button, as though the player were mechanically spinning the reels, when actually it is the number generator, constantly at work, that changes the draw every millisecond. The gambler is only selecting what is generated at the moment he pushes the button. Having lost, if he leaves his seat and sees the following player win, he might, so he tells himself, regret it, thinking he might have pocketed the gains had he stayed and played another few rounds. This incites the player to continue. Another way of creating the same feeling (“If I go on, I will win”) is to make the winning configuration appear next to the losing one that previously fell to the gambler.

舒尔极为详细地表明，感发的关键要素如何被整合进老虎机的软件与微处理器。例如，转轮给人一种印象，仿佛它们是因按下按钮而启动，好像玩家在机械地转动转轮；实际上，是持续运转的数字生成器每毫秒改变一次抽签结果。赌徒只是在按下按钮的那一刻选取已经生成的结果。输了之后，如果他离开座位，看到下一位玩家赢了，他可能会——他这样告诉自己——感到后悔，心想如果自己留下再多玩几轮，也许就把赢的钱收入囊中了。这就诱使玩家继续。制造同样感觉（“只要我继续，我就会赢”）的另一种办法，是让中奖组合出现在此前落在他头上的落败组合旁边。

The machine is programmed in such a way as to decide the rate at which funds are committed. Depending on the player’s usual strategies (duly recorded through data tracking and constantly recalculated), it can favor infrequent, big wins or, on the contrary, more limited and more frequent gains. However, eating away at gamblers’ money in small doses seems to be the surest way for the casino to pull in the profits. The continuous flux of small wins inexorably leads the gambler into the addiction zone, creating the illusion of false wins as the losses slowly accumulate.
机器的编程方式，决定了资金投入的速率。根据玩家惯常的策略（通过数据追踪被如实记录，并不断重新计算），它可以偏向罕见的大赢，或者相反，偏向更有限但更频繁的收益。然而，以小剂量蚕食赌徒的钱，似乎是赌场赚取利润最稳妥的方式。小额赢钱的持续流动，不可阻挡地把赌徒带入致瘾区域，在损失慢慢累积的同时制造虚假赢钱的幻觉。

The machine massively intervenes in the way the gambler feels his losses and wins. Affect is in the industry’s hands, with its computer experts, architects, designers, or experimental psychologists who, as one of them explains, work toward making the gambler functionally autistic: “You are the machine and the machine is you. Take leave of people.” This is attachment reaching its pinnacle. The machine is directly connected to mental states. The gambler is in the mousetrap. Innovations follow one another so that the gambler will give up any thought of calculating and finally let the machine play in his stead — twenty parallel poker games, or a hundred, if the gambler so wishes. The autoplay function confirms that what is left is only a programmed cyborg. The gambler does not even watch the cards anymore, only the counter that displays losses and wins. And soon he won’t even have to go to the machine anymore — the machine will come to him or, better, he will carry it with him. It will offer him what he likes and what he can no longer do without so as to carry him ever further from the world around him. He will have “blown the tab” for good.

机器在很大程度上介入赌徒感受输赢的方式。情动掌握在产业手中，掌握在其计算机专家、建筑师、设计师或实验心理学家手中；正如其中一位所解释的，他们的工作是让赌徒在功能上变得自闭（functionally autistic）：“你就是机器，机器就是你。与人告别吧。”这是附着达到了顶峰。机器与心理状态直接相连。赌徒落入了捕鼠器。创新接连不断，为的是让赌徒放弃任何计算的念头，最终让机器代替他玩——二十局并行的扑克，或者，如果赌徒愿意，一百局。自动游玩（autoplay）功能证实，剩下的只是一个被编程的赛博格。赌徒甚至不再看牌，只看显示输赢的计数器。很快，他甚至不必再走到机器跟前——机器会来到他身边，或者更好，他会把机器带在身上。机器会提供他所喜欢、他再也离不开的东西，好把他带得离周围世界越来越远。他将彻底“把珠子爆开”。

Addiction devices are spreading in a number of sectors and taking on greater importance. Indeed, many have observed that certain innovations in the gambling industry, such as biometric recognition or software dedicated to tracking fraudulent collusions, have been adapted in other sectors: airports, trading floors, insurance, banks, and the homeland security industry. One of the sectors where addiction devices have long played a central role is in food. In that case, what are shuffled are not card combinations, but rather combinations of sugar, fat, and salt calculated by mathematical models and validated by taste tests.

Then there are the dependency mechanisms that bind users through their body to their cell phones, screens, video games, and medicines, not to mention the traditional substances, tobacco and alcohol. In fact, the very notion of addiction has become a central category for marketing: the designers of the Blackpills application, which “creates, produces and diffuses short clips, engaged and radical, aimed at young adults and their cell phones,” make no bones about their objective to offer series that are “raw and addictive.”
致瘾装置正在若干部门扩散，并变得日益重要。的确，许多人观察到，赌博业的某些创新——例如生物特征识别，或专用于追踪欺诈性串通的软件——已被移植到其他部门：机场、交易大厅、保险、银行以及国土安全产业。致瘾装置长期扮演核心角色的部门之一，是食品业。在那里，被洗牌的不是纸牌组合，而是由数学模型计算、并经味觉测试验证的糖、脂肪与盐的组合。
还有那些通过身体把使用者与手机、屏幕、电子游戏和药物绑定在一起的依赖机制，更不用说烟草与酒精这些传统物质。事实上，成瘾这一概念本身已成为营销的核心范畴：Blackpills 应用的设计者——“创造、制作并传播短小、具有鲜明立场且激进、面向年轻成年人及其手机的短片”——毫不讳言其目标就是提供“生猛而令人上瘾”的剧集。

For the Romans, the word “addiction” referred to the state of a free man reduced to slavery because of debt. Echoing this etymology, we should go further and evoke the force and pervasiveness of the addiction devices linked to money and in particular to credit activities.

One of the most lucrative populations for lenders is that of the impecunious, living on the edge of the poverty level. They are the main customers for revolving loans, small sums borrowed over short periods at astronomical rates (300 percent APR). Well managed, this population can be made loyal, one loan after another, generating considerable revenue. How can this be achieved? To answer this question, sociologist Joe Deville analyzed Wonga’s success in the UK. Despite higher interest rates, Wonga surpassed the competition for several years, managing to durably attach its customers, who are poor and always in need of money.

Deville explains that Wonga never renegotiates contracts and refuses to extend existing loans. The rules of the game are that one has to have paid back the previous loan to get a new one. Just as the casino seeks out a gambler who pushes the button as many times as possible to renew the bet, the stakes for Wonga are gradually to establish the contours of a population that always lacks money but pays back the loans on time. No sugar, no salt or fat to lure and render dependent. Instead, there is a questionnaire and thirty criteria to fill out in five minutes online. Backstage, complicated calculations are made based on the mass of accumulated data in order to define behavioral profiles and identify, as the activities develop, those that correspond to the company’s target: the right borrower for this business model is poor and punctual. The Wonga customer learns to live with permanent debt that is repaid without fuss. He is dependent on the money lent by Wonga, and this dependence depends only on him, his behavior. If he stops paying back, he is free, but impoverished. Credit can be constructed like a slot machine that lends coins instead of swallowing them and that has learned, via questionnaires and algorithms, to carefully select a customer who will not be able to detach. The sequences are the same, with small sums that slowly generate large revenues and customers who behave properly so as to stay in the game: poor people who, because they are poor, are good candidates for repeat requests, poor people to whom the possibility of repetition is promised if they behave appropriately — in short, people who play the game and behave as they should. These, explains Deville, are the stakes of the relations Wonga establishes with its customers and to which it responds by setting up its calculation platforms and algorithms.
对罗马人而言，“addiction”（成瘾）一词指的是一个自由人因债务而沦为奴隶的状态。呼应这一词源，我们应当更进一步，考察那些与金钱、尤其与信贷活动相关的致瘾装置的力量与普遍性。

对放贷者来说，最有利可图的人群之一是囊中羞涩、生活在贫困线边缘的人。他们是循环贷款（revolving loans）的主要客户——小额借款，期限短，利率高得惊人（年化利率 APR 高达 300%）。若管理得当，这个人群可以被培养成忠实客户，一笔接一笔地借贷，带来可观的收入。如何做到这一点？为回答这个问题，社会学家乔·德维尔（Joe Deville）分析了 Wonga 在英国的成功。尽管利率更高，Wonga 仍在数年间超越竞争者，成功地持久附着住它的顾客——那些贫穷且总是需要钱的人。

德维尔解释说，Wonga 从不重新谈判合同，也拒绝展期现有贷款。游戏规则是：必须还清上一笔贷款，才能获得新贷款。正如赌场寻找一个尽可能多次按下按钮以续下赌注的赌徒，Wonga 的赌注是逐步勾勒出这样一个人群的轮廓：他们总是缺钱，却按时还款。没有糖、盐或脂肪来引诱并使人依赖。取而代之的，是一份问卷和三十项标准，可在网上用五分钟填写完毕。在后台，基于大量积累的数据进行复杂的计算，以界定行为画像，并随着业务发展识别出符合公司目标的人：适合这一商业模式的借款人是贫穷而按时还款的人。Wonga 的顾客学会与永久债务共处，不声不响地偿还。他依赖于 Wonga 借出的钱，而这种依赖只取决于他、取决于他的行为。如果他停止还款，就摆脱了这种依赖，却也更为贫困。信贷可以被构造得像一台老虎机：它借出硬币而不是吞下硬币，并已通过问卷与算法学会精心挑选一个无法脱离的顾客。序列是相同的：小额款项慢慢产生大笔收入，顾客为了留在游戏中而循规蹈矩：穷人，因为贫穷，是重复申请的好人选；穷人，只要行为得当，就被许诺重复的可能性——简言之，是那些参与游戏并照规矩行事的人。德维尔解释说，这些就是 Wonga 与其顾客所建立之关系的赌注，而 Wonga 正是通过建立其计算平台与算法来回应这些赌注。
José Ossandon further confirms how efficient these addiction devices are in his work on the growth of credit cards provided to their customers by the large distribution companies in Mexico.

Cards that serve as means of payment can also be used to obtain cash and contract miniloans at very high interest rates. Their holders can lend these cards to family members or friends. The companies that emit these devices run nonnegligible, but statistically manageable risks. Like Wonga, their aim is to enact consumers that behave in accordance with their business model — that is, those who repay on time and to whom one can renew loans. This case is particularly interesting because it attests to a phenomenon of growing importance: the emergence and development of private monies, in this case, shared by the holders and users of the card, on one side, and, on the other side, those who emit the cards. Ossandon convincingly shows that these monies take hold of those who use them, gradually creating dependency. A credit card is a self-reinforcing device that attaches by making dependent: the more you use it, the more you will use it again.
何塞·奥桑东（José Ossandon）在研究墨西哥大型分销公司向其顾客提供的信用卡增长时，进一步确认了这些致瘾装置何等有效。

作为支付手段的信用卡，也可用来获取现金，并以极高利率订立小额贷款合同。持卡人可以把卡借给家人或朋友。发行这些装置的公司承担着不可忽视、但在统计上可控的风险。像 Wonga 一样，它们的目标是造就按自身商业模式行事的消费者——也就是按时还款、可以不断续贷的人。这个案例特别有趣，因为它见证了一个日益重要的现象：私人货币（private monies）的兴起与发展——在此情形中，私人货币由持卡人与用卡者一方，与发卡者另一方共享。奥桑东令人信服地表明，这些货币攫住了使用它们的人，逐渐制造依赖。信用卡是一种自我强化的装置，通过使人依赖而实现附着：你越是用它，你就越会再次用它。
MORE AND MORE ATTACHING ATTACHMENTS?
越来越具附着力的附着？

Successful attachments imply some form of conversation, coproduction of goods, and addiction. For example, in Las Vegas, those who design the gambling space regularly take tours of the floor to interview their gamblers. They organize focus groups, and working closely with the gamblers, they polish the ergonomics of the “zone.”

No addiction device can do without conversation and coconception or coconception rooted in conversation. No doubt the inverse also holds. Without recourse to coconception or to mechanisms that create dependencies, attachments would be so fragile as to be imperiled, along with the profits they generate. Nevertheless, the combinations that allow for a great diversity in the commercial strategies are infinite. They play on the more or less partial and ephemeral nature of attaching.
成功的附着意味着某种形式的对话、物品的共同生产以及成瘾。例如，在拉斯维加斯，设计赌博空间的人会定期巡视赌场大厅，访谈他们的赌客。他们组织焦点小组，并与赌客紧密合作，打磨“区域”（zone）的人体工学设计。
任何致瘾装置都离不开对话与共同构想，或者说，离不开植根于对话的共同构想。无疑，反过来也成立。若不借助共同构想，或不借助那些制造依赖的机制，附着就会脆弱得岌岌可危，连同其所产生的利润也一并岌岌可危。然而，使商业策略呈现巨大多样性的组合是无穷无尽的。它们所利用的，是附着或多或少带有局部性与短暂性这一特点。

My sense is that addiction devices aiming to trigger durable dependent behaviors are increasingly important in the production of commercial attachments in what is usually called capitalist markets. In this case, addiction and profit seem closely linked and dependent on one another. Addiction is therefore becoming a central category in the social sciences, even if it is historically contingent.
Anthropologist Paul Rabinow considers addiction a starting point for thinking about today’s
anthropos

Engineering addiction and addictive practices makes explicit and weaves together on a whole new scale the stuff that contemporary man is made from. The range and degrees of addiction extend every day, each good finding the agencies it will take and each agency the goods on which it will depend.
我的感觉是，在通常所谓的资本主义市场中，旨在触发持久依赖行为的致瘾装置，在商业附着的生产中正变得越来越重要。在这种情况下，成瘾与利润似乎紧密相连、彼此依赖。因此，成瘾正成为社会科学中的一个核心范畴，尽管它取决于特定的历史条件。
人类学家保罗·拉比诺（Paul Rabinow）把成瘾视为思考今日的“人”（
anthropos
）的一个起点。
对成瘾及成瘾实践的工程化，把构成当代人的材料在一个全新的尺度上加以显明，并编织到一起。成瘾的范围与程度每天都在扩展：每一件物品都找到它所要吸纳的能动者，而每一个能动者也找到它所依赖的物品。

I cannot draw these remarks to a close without evoking the question of detachments. It is as important on the supply side as on the demand side to manage affects that make the agents act. I have already raised this issue in the case of listening and coproduction devices. With addiction devices, however, this issue of detachment takes on a whole new dimension and becomes a constant source of worry. As Schüll’s interviews with designers and engineers show, they also find pleasure in the gaming industry. There is pleasure in tracking and above all in capturing the gambler, snatching him from the clutches of competitors without ruining him: the customer must live. The greater the hold machines have and the more gamblers’ dependency increases, the more those on the supply side exult. They also exult when they win a court case brought by a state that accuses them of not truly respecting the laws of chance in the way they decide upon losing configurations. We would need a Hannah Arendt to account for the banality of evil in a situation where responsibility is put on those whom the device aims to make less responsible in an economy of affects in which exultation is exchanged for dependency with consent. In order to avoid public opprobrium, the gambling industry finances both treatment centers for dependent gamblers and research to identify those gamblers most likely to fall into irreversible dependency — just as mobile phone providers hire psychologists to explain to parents how to manage their children and their mobiles. Likewise, the food industry employs battalions of dieticians to convince consumers not to overconsume the products they offer, and public powers set up commissions for the overindebted to wean them off credit. Market attachment produces concerns that will haunt us for quite a while and will make market agencements subject to debate.

在结束这些论述之前，我不能不提及脱离的问题。无论供给侧还是需求侧，管理那些促使行动者行动的情动都同样重要。在倾听装置与共同生产装置的情形中，我已经提出过这个问题。然而，在致瘾装置这里，脱离问题呈现出全新的维度，并成为持续忧虑的来源。正如舒尔（Schüll）对设计师与工程师的访谈所显示的，他们也在博彩业中寻得乐趣。追踪赌客，尤其是俘获赌客——把他从竞争对手的手中夺过来，又不把他毁掉——这其中自有乐趣：顾客必须活下去。机器的掌控力越大，赌客的依赖越深，供给侧的人就越是欢欣鼓舞。当某个州指控他们在决定输局组合的方式上没有真正尊重随机法则、而他们却赢下这场诉讼时，他们同样欢欣鼓舞。我们需要一位汉娜·阿伦特（Hannah Arendt），才能解释这样一种处境中的恶之平庸：责任被推到那些人身上，而装置恰恰意在削弱他们自主负责的能力；在这种情动经济中，欢腾换来的，是经当事人同意的依赖。为了避免公众的谴责，博彩业既资助针对成瘾赌客的治疗中心，也资助研究，以识别那些最可能陷入不可逆依赖的赌客——正如移动电话运营商聘请心理学家，向父母解释如何管理孩子及其手机。同样，食品业雇用大批营养师，说服消费者不要过度消费它们提供的产品；公共权力机构则为过度负债者设立委员会，帮助他们戒除信贷。市场附着所产生的关切，将在相当长一段时间里困扰我们，并使市场装配成为争论的对象。

The challenge that market agencements must meet in constantly renewed ways is to lead someone all the way to the point that they consent to pay to acquire it. Without taking into account the world of passions, it would be impossible to understand how this challenge can be met: the
affectio mercatus

stimulates trust, but also, even more fundamentally, it agitates, heats, perks up, as marketers would say, and pushes agents to consider that they cannot do without the good being offered. To explain how these connections are made, we saw that one has to give up the convenient hypothesis according to which goods and agents are exterior to one another and instead put their conjoined evolution at the center of the analysis. It is over the course of this evolution and the explorations it provokes that a bundle of interdependencies are eventually woven that attach the good to the one for whom it was destined. The agent is affected by the good (
affecté par
) at the same time as they are assigned to it (
affecté à
). This double movement requires that agencies and goods be simultaneously engaged; the various modalities of this engagement led me to distinguish three families of attachment devices.
市场装配必须不断以新的方式应对的挑战，是把某个人一路引导到同意支付以购得它的地步。若不把激情世界纳入考虑，就无法理解这一挑战如何能够得到应对：市场情动（
affectio mercatus
）激发信任，但更根本的是，它还搅动、加热、使人振奋——用营销人员的话说——并推动行动者认为自己离不开所提供的物品。为解释这些连接如何形成，我们已经看到，必须放弃那个便利的假设——物品与行动者彼此外在——转而把二者共同的演化置于分析的中心。正是在这一演化过程及其所引发的探索之中，一束相互依赖关系最终被编织起来，把物品附着到它为之预定的那个人身上。行动者受到物品的影响（
affecté par
），同时又被指派给它（
affecté à
）。这一双重运动要求能动者与物品同时被卷入；这种卷入的各种模态，使我区分出三类附着装置。

No matter the type of device, the practical framing of affects is a permanent invention. There is neither a best way nor a universal solution: it all depends on the good and the agents involved. This explains why success is never guaranteed and why, when it seems to have been achieved, it often turns out to be incomplete and temporary. Through the framings they impose, devices provoke reactions and protest. Attachment, as the word says, is not far from the act of taking hold, which can generate resistance.
无论装置属于何种类型，对情动的实际框定都是一项永不停息的发明。既没有最佳方式，也没有普遍解决方案：一切都取决于所涉的物品与行动者。这解释了为什么成功从无保证，也解释了为什么当成功似乎已经达成时，它往往又显得不完整、不持久。装置通过其强加的框定，引发反应与抗议。附着，正如这个词本身所示，离“抓住”的行为并不远，而抓住可能招致抵抗。

Thus, the devices conceived to attach consumers are subject to constant criticism. For instance: “Advertisement is full of lies and degradation; algorithms with their data and databases are reductive and produce a travesty of reality and real needs. The coproduction of goods is an illusion and participation a mirage: Who can claim that all consumers are heard? Who would dare assert that what they say or ask for is really taken into account? There are countless solicitations that are ignored, repressed, or forgotten.” As for the actual addiction, it provokes flashes of lucidity, indignant protests, and calls for resistance against the risks of enslavement and decay. In fact, each attachment strategy can be used by agents as a resource to denounce the limits of others. For instance: “Why was I never told about this good on which I am now dependent? Why was I not explicitly involved in its design?” Or again: “Why settle for organizing an amiable conversation about this substance, as though there were nothing special to say about the risk of addiction?” In the face of these ever more complex and problematic movements brought about by the multiplication of attachment devices, the control of the delicate chemistry and the subtle logistics of affectations become a strategic stake.

因此，那些为附着消费者而构想的装置，不断受到批评。例如：“广告充满谎言与堕落；算法连同其数据与数据库，是化约式的，制造出对现实与真实需要的扭曲写照。物品的共同生产是幻象，参与是海市蜃楼：谁能声称所有消费者都被倾听？谁又敢断言，他们所说或所求真的被考虑在内？无数诉求被无视、被压制或被遗忘。”至于成瘾本身，它会引发阵阵清醒、愤慨的抗议，以及针对奴役与衰败风险的反抗呼声。事实上，每一种附着策略都可以被行动者用作资源，去谴责其他策略的局限。例如：“为什么从来没有人告诉过我有关这件我现在所依赖的物品的情况？为什么没有明确让我参与它的设计？”又或者：“为什么只满足于围绕这种物质组织一场亲切的对话，仿佛关于成瘾风险并没有什么特别的话可说？”面对附着装置的增殖所带来的这些日益复杂、日益成问题的动态，对感发作用（affectations）的精妙化学与微妙物流的控制，便成为一项战略赌注。
